task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and an explainer of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers answering why some bags labeled compostable are not accepted in Elmharbor's food-scrap bins. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Elmharbor collection service sends food scraps to one contracted processing site with a specified list of accepted materials.
The current collection list permits loose food scraps, plain paper liners and the uncoated paper bags distributed through the city program.
The processor does not currently accept plastic-like compostable bags, even when the packaging carries a general compostability claim.
The processor's operating note says its screening and processing schedule are not set up to distinguish and handle every certified bag formulation.
The city's rule describes what this contracted system can accept and is not a finding that every excluded bag's label is fraudulent.
Collection manager Enna Pell said, "Our crews need a rule they can apply to the material in the bin, not a packaging claim they have time to research at the curb."
Residents asked for clarification after shops began stocking several differently labeled liners beside ordinary garbage bags.
The city and participating shops will display the local acceptance list together rather than suggest that a retail shelf category determines collection eligibility.
Food-scrap bins containing unaccepted packaging may receive a notice asking the user to remove it before the next ordinary collection.
A rejected bin is not automatically a fine, and the city has not announced a new financial penalty in this clarification.
Apartment managers can request a demonstration session for shared-bin users because an individual resident may not know who added a contaminating item.
Apartment manager Roven Dale said, "A notice on the lid reaches the next person who opens it, not necessarily the person who put the bag there."
The processor reports contamination by incoming load, which does not identify a particular household or establish the habits of all residents.
The supplied record contains no citywide percentage of correctly sorted bins or quantified benefit from this clarification.
The city will review the accepted-material list if the processor's equipment or contract changes.
A manufacturer may submit product information for that review, but a submission does not immediately change what collectors accept.
The food-scrap service remains separate from ordinary recycling, so excluded liners should not automatically be placed in the recycling bin.
The city's waste guide provides the current route for excluded packaging and will be updated alongside the bin notices.
The paper liners are optional; households may use the city's listed loose-scrap collection method without buying them.
The processor uses finished material in contracted landscaping work after its ordinary quality checks, not as a guaranteed product returned to each contributing household.
Several community gardens display their own compost rules, which can differ because they use a different small-scale process.
The clarification does not require every community garden to adopt the municipal processor's acceptance list.

forbidden_additions: All compostability labels declared false or all labeled bags accepted.
A new fine, a citywide sorting-success rate or automatic recycling of excluded liners.
Mandatory purchase of city paper bags.
preserve: Product claims distinguished from a particular collection and processing system's rules.
The limits of load-level evidence and the practical shared-bin problem.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
